title: Cross-Country Skiing Foundation Strength

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Slow, controlled spinal movement. Arch and round back fully.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cues: Sit tall, keep chest up while rotating between hip positions.

items.name: Banded Shoulder Dislocates
items.cues: Use light band, keep arms straight, focus on shoulder mobility.

items.name: Bear Crawl
items.cues: Keep hips low, core tight. Move opposite hand and foot together.

items.name: Back Squat
items.cues: Descend to parallel, drive through heels. Keep chest up and core braced.

items.name: Bent Over Row
items.cues: Hinge at hips, pull bar to lower chest. Squeeze shoulder blades together.

items.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
items.cues: Front leg does the work. Descend straight down, drive up through heel.

items.name: Cable Pull-Through
items.cues: Hip hinge movement, keep back neutral. Drive hips forward to stand.

items.name: Bird Dog
items.cues: Extend opposite arm and leg. Hold 2 seconds, keep hips level.

items.name: Calf Stretch
items.cues: Keep back leg straight, lean forward into wall. Feel stretch in calf.

items.name: Biceps Wall Stretch
items.cues: Place palm on wall, turn body away. Keep arm straight.

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Slow, gentle movement to decompress spine after loading.

rationale: Foundation strength workout targeting key muscle groups needed for Vasaloppet skiing - legs, back, and core stability
Moderate intensity (RPE 6-7) appropriate for building strength base 54 days out from race without excessive fatigue
Functional movement patterns that translate to skiing biomechanics - hip hinge, single leg stability, and posterior chain strength
